where: Section 1, sentence after the power formula
problem: "Energy is power over time" is ambiguous English. A second-language reader can read "over" as division (P ÷ t), which would give the wrong unit for kWh.
fix: Write: "Energy is power multiplied by time: E = P × t, in kilowatt-hours (kWh), with P in kW and t in hours."

problem: "so idle servers waste most of the power" does not follow clearly from the number just shown. The 260 W is a loaded server, not an idle one; the reader needs the point that the 200 W idle part, not the 60 W load part, is the big share.
fix: Write: "At u = 0.3 the idle floor alone is 200 W of the 260 W drawn, about 77 percent, so on lightly loaded servers most of the power goes on keeping the host alive, not on doing work."

problem: The pointer to Chapter 4.6 is plain text, so on a phone it is not tappable like the other chapter cross-references in the series.
fix: Make it a chapter link, for example: See Chapter 4.6 for replication trade-offs.
